sentences.text: Researchers employed a cohort design involving 141 treatment-naive neuroblastoma patients to evaluate eleven machine-learning models that combined six non-invasive clinical and blood-based markers for predicting disease risk.

During the training phase, the random forest algorithm correctly classified 91 percent of patients, with image-defined risk factors, neuron-specific enolase, and lactate dehydrogenase emerging as the most important variables for the prediction.

When tested on a separate group, the final model maintained high accuracy with a sensitivity of 84.2 percent, leading the authors to conclude that this method offers a practical way to classify neuroblastoma risk without needing to analyze tumor tissue.
